summary: This chunk adds a new file, benchmark.json, recording eval results for the adversarial-review-2 skill. It runs eval 1 and eval 2 twice each: once with_skill, once without_skill. All four configurations pass every expectation except without_skill/eval_id 2, which fails the retest-mechanism check. with_skill scores a perfect 1.0 mean pass rate on both evals but takes far longer (~1191s mean vs ~101s) and uses roughly double the tokens (~62.7k vs ~31.4k). A run_summary block aggregates mean/stddev/min/max per configuration and states deltas: pass_rate +0.08, time_seconds +1090.1, tokens +31278, all favoring without_skill on cost and with_skill on pass rate.

claims.text: with_skill eval 1 passed 7/7 expectations, pass_rate 1.0, took 1178.8s, used 62950 tokens, 10 tool calls, 1 error
with_skill eval 2 passed 6/6 expectations, pass_rate 1.0, took 1203.5s, used 62457 tokens, 10 tool calls, 1 error
without_skill eval 1 passed 7/7 expectations, pass_rate 1.0, took 120.6s, used 33200 tokens, 5 tool calls, 0 errors
without_skill eval 2 passed 5/6 expectations, pass_rate 0.83, took 81.5s, used 29650 tokens, 4 tool calls, 0 errors

The one failing expectation across all runs is 'Report contains a retest list or equivalent re-check mechanism' for without_skill eval 2, because the report's 'Bottom line' section lists remediations rather than a mechanism to re-verify findings after fixes
Both with_skill runs hit a harness guard that blocked the Write tool for report.md, so the executor wrote it via a Bash/shell heredoc instead, which is the one recorded error in each run's metrics

run_summary aggregates show with_skill mean pass_rate 1.0 (stddev 0.0), mean time 1191.15s, mean tokens 62703.5; without_skill mean pass_rate 0.915 (stddev 0.1202), mean time 101.05s, mean tokens 31425.0
Delta block states pass_rate +0.08, time_seconds +1090.1, tokens +31278 (with_skill minus without_skill)

risks.note: The analyzer_model field is explicitly unrecorded, so grading provenance for these pass/fail calls is not established in this chunk.
Only 1 run per configuration is recorded, so the without_skill stddev of 0.1202 in pass_rate is computed from just two data points (eval 1 and eval 2), which is a thin sample for a variance claim.

least_confident: I could not verify from this chunk alone whether the without_skill runs and with_skill runs graded the same underlying report artifacts fairly, since the reports themselves and the grading rubric live outside this chunk.
